method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING, or a NOTHING-kind answer, where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; two regulative rules (the law practice's bar on suing before the days of s 289 (1) and s 292 (6), (7) have passed; the client's 12 months to apply for a costs assessment, s 294A (5)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Legal Profession Act 2006 (ACT), A2006-25, Republication No 45 (R45), effective 16 May 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A2006-25.txt; the s 281 (4) (b) rate from the Court Procedures Rules 2006 (SL2006-29), schedule 2, items 2.3 and 2.4, as deposited at subjects/au/act/court-procedures-rules-2006/registers/source-bundle/SL2006-29.txt

seat: the client: the person who retains a lawyer (a law practice) for a matter, such as a personal injury, workers compensation, will or discrimination claim, and pays or is asked to pay the legal costs (lpact-costs.l4)
focus: costs agreements: Division 3.2.5 whole, with the costs disclosure, billing, suing and assessment machinery of Part 3.2 around it

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run lpact-dates.l4 ; l4 run lpact-costs.l4 ; l4 run lpact-cases.l4
checks.result: 154 assertions written, 154 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07); a deliberately wrong assertion in a scratch copy showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Part 3.2 for the client. In: s 261 (definitions used), ss 263-265 (application), s 269 with ss 271, 272, 275 (disclosure and its exceptions), s 274, s 277, s 278 (1), (2), s 279, s 281, Division 3.2.5 whole (ss 282-288), s 289, s 292, s 294A (1), (3)-(7), s 298 (b), s 300C, s 302, ss 304, 304A, s 307A. Out: ss 266-268 (but s 268 (2) in an answer), 270, 273, 276, 278 (3), (4), third party payers (ss 261A, 278A, 294A (2), (8)-(10)), ss 280, 286, 290-291 (asked as one fact), 293, 295-297, 299-301, 303, the offences (ss 284 (6), (7), 285 (3), (4)), machinery (ss 262, 305-307), the Civil Law (Wrongs) Act 2002 caps. Reasons in NOTES.md.
